paper_title: Particle dispersion in the classical vector dark matter background
notes: Phenomenology paper deriving NEW bounds on light vector DM (gauged U(1)) from the medium-induced modification of particle dispersion/normalization in the classical vector-DM background. Headline canonical result reported here: the dark photon model (Fig. 6, fig:DPBounds). The paper's own new dark-photon constraints are the dashed green (delta m_e^oplus, Eq. 35) and dashed black (Z-normalization, Eq. 39) lines. Over the whole plotted range (m < ~5 MeV) the black Z line is the more stringent upper bound and defines the boundary of the paper's new excluded region; the abstract/text emphasize this normalization bound as ruling out 'a huge region of the VDM parameter space'. Eq. 39: g_psi < 6.6e-39 (m_gamma'/1e-20 eV)^2 (0.3 GeV cm^-3 / rho)^{1/2}. For the dark photon the electron effective coupling is g_e = eps*e (e = sqrt(4*pi*alpha) = 0.3028), so chi = eps = g_psi/e = 2.18e-38 (m/1e-20 eV)^2 at rho=0.3 GeV/cm^3. Excluded region is chi ABOVE this rising line; curve truncated at chi=1. Bound is an order-of-magnitude estimate (2-sigma refers to the assumed local DM density 0.3 GeV/cm^3); no formal statistical CL is quoted, 0.95 recorded as nominal. Density-dependent DM bound reported at the paper's native rho=0.3, not rescaled. Other headline model (L_mu-L_tau) and B-L (Fig. 5) are not reported here as they are outside/less-central to the canonical DarkPhoton plane; brown DPDM region in Fig. 6 is borrowed from prior work, not the paper's own derivation.
